Hello <@&661392170472701995> , and a huge, heartfelt welcome to the "Forgotten Ones" campaign!

I have been absolutely blown away by the creativity and depth of the characters you all submitted. My original plan was to select three players for this journey, but your applications were so unique, compelling, and full of narrative potential that I couldn't possibly turn any of you away.

Therefore, I am thrilled to officially announce that all four of you have been accepted!

**Varda, Vena, Vosk, and Dryzan** will soon be awakening from a long, cold sleep alongside **Wes Del-Fin** to unravel the mysteries of their shared predicament. The sheer breadth of history and experience represented by this group promises an incredible story.

**What's Next?**

Please keep an eye out for the following in the coming days as we get ready for the Prelude and character finalization:

* **Private DM Threads:** I will create individual private DM threads for each of you within our <#1380214441328509100> channel. This will be a space for us to discuss your character's secrets and personal story arcs one-on-one. 

* **Character Generation Guide:** The link to our wiki's guide for character creation, which will contain all the house rules, level information, and other resources you'll need.

* **Character Sheet:** The Google Sheets Character Sheet template that we will be using for the campaign.

Thank you all again for your passion and creativity. I am beyond excited to begin this adventure with you all. Welcome to the crew!

Excited to get to know all of your characters!

***The staff of far-seeing*** (working title)

Varda had run with Lyrus to a remote world in the outer rim, Backlash for helping her Mandalorian friend Araden Kryz. It was a small world with one or two towns. As they were settling Varda looked away for a second and Lyrus vanished. She began searching through the Force desperate, unraveling, following the fragile spark of growing life she knew by heart. But instead of that familiar thread, her senses caught something else. Something ancient. Its signature was unlike anything she had felt before, warmth kissed by shadow, clarity wrapped in mist. It did not call to her… but it did not hide either.

She followed it across narrow streets and quiet alleys. There, in a crooked vendor's stall, she found it: a shaft of weathered wood, hanging unceremoniously on a wall among trinkets and junk. Yet the Force clung to it. Saturated it.

When she asked, the vendor chuckled and claimed it had been in his family for generations, “My grandfather’s grandfather’s,” he said. “Came from a world no one ever visits anymore… called Atollon.” The name meant nothing to her, but the feel of it stirred something deep. She asked the price.

He winked. “For you, no charge.”

Varda took the wood and ran past her grandson smiling. She looked at the wood then to him and smiled back. Under starlight she began to carve. Slowly. Reverently. She shaped it into a cane of elegant lines and jagged symbols of twilight, spirals of storm and the eye that sees in stillness. With her grandson by her side. She taught him to feel the weft. To feel how the force flowed through it. 

Then she returned, the danger subsided. Her Mandalorian friend, in gratitude for rescuing his daughter, gifted her three rings of beskar, which she inlaid into the heart of the staff. One for endurance. One for clarity. One for balance.

It is a tether to the middle ground, a conduit of vision, not always of what will be, but of what could. It hums softly when twilight falls. It vibrates when the Force is disturbed. And sometimes, when she dreams, she sees the storm again, the storm with no side.

### **Varda's Wound: The Echo of Darkness**

The experience has left Varda with a profound and permanent "wound" that is both physical and spiritual.

* **A Scarred Force Connection:** The raw dark side energy she absorbed didn't vanish. It settled within her, creating a permanent scar on her connection to the Force. Now, every time she uses her magick, she feels an echo of that agonizing moment. This manifests as:
    * **Chronic Pain:** A dull, persistent ache in her bones, like a constant pressure from within, that occasionally flares into sharp, stabbing pains during moments of stress or when she draws deeply on the Force.
    * **Spiritual Dissonance:** Her "purified" magick is now constantly at war with the raw, chaotic darkness she contains. This results in a form of spiritual static. Her visions may be more powerful but are now often tainted with violent or terrifying imagery. She might misinterpret feelings, sensing hostility where there is only fear, or vice-versa.

* **The Constant Temptation:** The darkness she holds is not just a painful memory; it is a tool. It whispers to her, offering her the "quick and easy path" that she has sworn to reject. In moments of desperation, she might be tempted to unleash this raw power—a quicker, more brutal solution than the difficult, balanced path she has chosen. This is her core internal conflict: using her carefully controlled, purified abilities while fighting against the seductive, destructive power she holds captive within herself.

*   **Mechanic:** Immediately after Varda uses a **Force Power**, the contained dark energy makes an attack against her.
*   **Attack Roll vs. Fortitude Defense:** The attack roll is made against Varda's own **Fortitude Defense**.

### ** The Sundered Core** ###

The mortal injury that led to your long sleep was catastrophic. Though the advanced stasis process sealed the wound and saved your life, it did not truly heal it. You bear the scars of a lightsaber **piercing clean through your abdomen**—a small, puckered entry wound on your stomach and a larger, ragged exit scar on your back. They are a constant, physical reminder of a moment of ultimate failure. The wound pulls with every twist of your torso, an ache that flares to sharp pain with overexertion. You feel as though you are held together by will as much as by flesh.

More than just a physical mark, the weapon that delivered the blow left a "cold spot" in your soul. It’s a place of metaphysical numbness in your connection to the Force, a permanent vulnerability you can feel whenever dark energies are near.

Your Mandalorian iron will, however, allows you to push past the pain in moments of desperation, to perform incredible feats when everything is on the line. But you know that such effort takes its toll on your damaged core, threatening to tear the old wound open and leaving you staggering and weakened in its aftermath.

### **Wes's Wound: Final Game Mechanics** ###

#### **1. The Cold Scar** ####

The dark side energy of the Inquisitor's lightsaber left a permanent spiritual vulnerability.

* **Mechanic:** Wes suffers a persistent **-2 penalty to his Will Defense**, but only against Force Powers that have the **[dark side]** descriptor.

#### **2. Unstable Core** ####

Pushing his body to its absolute limit risks tearing the delicate, stasis-mended tissues of his wound.

* **Ability Name:** **Iron Will**
* **Activation:** Once per encounter, as a **Free Action**, Wes may choose to **re-roll** one failed **attack roll, Athletics check, or Endurance check**. He must accept the result of the second roll.
* **The Cost:** Immediately after using this ability, he moves **-1 step down the Condition Track**. This is a normal penalty and can be removed via the Recovery action.

### **Signature Item: The "Pathfinder" Field Jacket**

**Lore and Description**
A custom-made explorer's jacket in a distinct, bright green color. It appears to be simple, durable synth-leather, but it's actually a piece of high-end corporate or military scout gear that Iyola likely "acquired" or won in a challenge. It's designed for survival and data gathering in hostile environments.

**Reinforced Weave:** The jacket's hardy materials provide a **+2 equipment bonus to Fortitude Defense**.
**Explorer's Pockets:** It is fitted with **5 reinforced, shielded pockets/compartments**, each capable of holding items up to 0.5kg without creating an obvious bulge.

** Environmental Acuity**
* *The jacket is interwoven with micro-sensors and environmentally reactive fibers that heighten the wearer's already keen senses, allowing them to pick up on subtle changes in the environment.*
* **Mechanical Benefit:** Once per encounter, as a **swift action**, Iyola can activate the jacket's sensor suite. When she does, she gains a **+5 equipment bonus** on the next **Perception** or **Survival** check she makes before the end of her turn.
* **Gameplay Effect:** This represents a moment of intense focus where the jacket helps her spot a hidden trap, notice a camouflaged creature, find a subtle trail, or identify an atmospheric hazard, perfectly complementing her high base skills in Perception and Survival.

**Daredevil's Weave**
* *The jacket is crafted from a unique synth-weave that can momentarily stiffen to absorb and disperse kinetic energy from a sudden, heavy impact.*
* **Mechanical Benefit:** Once per day, when Iyola would be moved down the **Condition Track** as a result of taking damage (i.e., when damage exceeds her damage threshold), she can use this ability as a **Reaction**. When she does, she reduces the number of steps she moves down the Condition Track by one (to a minimum of zero).

You may now begin posting in your individual introduction threads whenever you are ready. As you formulate your first posts, please keep the following in-game mechanical effects in mind.

### **Starting Condition: Hibernation Sickness**

You are all awakening from a slumber that has lasted for centuries, and the process has left your bodies and minds in a fragile state. This is represented by a **Persistent Condition** called Hibernation Sickness, which has two primary effects:

1.  **-2 Steps on the Condition Track:** You begin the game at -2 steps on the Condition Track. This imposes a **-2 penalty on all of your attack rolls, ability checks, and skill checks.**
2.  **Blinded:** Your vision is gone, replaced by a disorienting darkness. Mechanically, this means:
    *   You have a **-2 penalty to your Reflex Defense** and you **lose your Dexterity bonus to Reflex.**
    *   You move at **half speed.**
    *   You take a **-5 penalty on Perception checks.**
    *   All opponents have **Total Concealment** from you.
    *   Any check that relies on vision automatically fails.

This is a Persistent Condition and will not fade quickly on its own.

---

### **For Force-Sensitive Characters:** ###

Though your eyes have failed you, the Force can provide another kind of sight. Without training, however, you will not be able to read screens without significant focus.

*   **Force Sight:** As a **Swift Action**, you may make a **DC 20 Use the Force check**. If you succeed, you can perceive your surroundings through the Force, removing the penalties from blindness on your Perception checks until the start of your next turn.
*   **Sustained Sight:** Outside of combat, one successful check allows you to maintain this Force Sight for about ten minutes before you need to refocus.

---

But it might also be borne out in little things, like that she naturally has the "violence is my last resort" mindset and thinks Jedi are awesome.

I had considered something along those lines back before but usually players who generally don't start with force sensitive ever really want to delve into Force stuff.

With Dryzan now an ancillary character and Iyola now the only non forcey of the group it may make for interesting character development for Iyola to be a latent force sensitive.
I figured it might give you a few more plot options if need be. It's also an interesting character thing if it ever comes up.

So, we’re going to weave in a subtle, unconscious connection to the Force that’s been part of her all along, without needing the "Force Sensitivity" feat just yet.

Think of it like this:

You know how Iyola is unusually mobile, quick on her feet, and seems to land gracefully even when things get chaotic? Or how she picks up new languages almost instinctively? We're going to lean into that. It’s not "magic," as far as she's concerned, but sometimes, things just seem to *happen* for her. A lucky roll, a quick jump that prevents a fall, or just picking up a new word faster than she should. It's her little edge, and she probably just thinks she's naturally awesome, or maybe has crazy good reflexes. We'll use moments like this to highlight that subtle connection.

She won't be able to consciously use the Force like a Jedi. She won't have Force powers, or even "sense" Force users in a clear way. Instead, sometimes she might get a strong impression from someone's intense emotions – like a gut feeling that something's really off, or someone is genuinely distraught. And in those very specific, intense moments, if someone is thinking a name or a single word with incredible focus, she might just "hear" it, like a faint whisper in the back of her mind, or almost like a stray thought that wasn't hers. It’s not mind-reading; it’s more like catching a particularly strong thought echo.

I'll look for natural moments in the story for these little nudges to happen, usually when things are really intense for a character around her. You can then interpret these subtle feelings as you like! Maybe she takes a guess, or has a sudden, uncanny "hunch," or even (as you cleverly suggested!) claims she "lip-read" something when a name pops into her head. It’s all about *her* perception and how she explains these improbable insights.

This is purely a narrative and roleplaying element for now, adding depth and mystery to Iyola's character.
You won't get extra skill bonuses or Force powers from this right now. If, down the line, you decide to fully embrace this and want to gain mechanical Force abilities, you'd then take the "Force Sensitivity" feat.

Think of it as adding another layer to the "Explorer's Gambit" wound, deepening her unique path through this adventure. Does that sound like a fun and fair way to explore this?

The first few minutes yield nothing but dust-free synth-steel and the quiet hum of the ship. 

Her eyes then fall upon a wall panel near the lowest bunk, closest to the door. It appears perfectly flush, but her keen gaze, trained to spot the minutest inconsistencies, catches a faint discoloration in the metal. It's almost imperceptible, a ghost of a residue that has been vigorously scrubbed away. Pressing closer, she can just barely make out the faintest, almost vanished outlines of what were once childish crayon marks or finger paints – primitive stick figures, crude renderings of what might be starships or fantastical beasts. They're layered, some attempting to cover others, suggesting years of a child's ephemeral art, eventually erased. The image speaks of two distinct hand-sizes, two different, very young artistic styles. It's a subtle but poignant ghost of two childhoods.

Iyola continues her meticulous sweep, running her hands along every surface, her fingers probing every seam. She checks behind the flush comm panel, then pries open the maintenance access for the environmental controls, her sharp eyes scanning every crevice. There, tucked deep within a narrow, forgotten space, almost as if deliberately concealed yet carelessly overlooked, she finds it: a small, sturdy, non-metallic, woven pouch. It feels old, worn, soft with age, a surprising contrast to the ship's metallic surfaces.

Carefully, she extracts the pouch. It contains a small collection of sentimental treasures, childish but clearly cherished. There's a polished, perfectly smooth river stone, warm to the touch; a single, intricately braided strand of hair (one brown, one almost black, tied together); and, most remarkably, a small, very old, fragmented flimsiplast holopicture.

The holopicture is faded, its colors muted by time, and slightly warped from what looks like prolonged dampness at some point in its distant past. The background is slightly out of focus, depicting a verdant landscape with subtle, terraced buildings nestled into the side of a distant mountain, and broad, green plains stretching out before them under a soft, diffused sunlight—a landscape utterly unlike Bespin or any other known, common galactic world.

In the foreground, however, the figures are clear, despite the picture's age. It's an image of a young woman, perhaps in her mid-twenties, with rich brown hair and startlingly bright blue eyes, her lips curved in a gentle, almost secret smile. On her hip, clearly visible, hangs a lightsaber, its hilt gleaming faintly. She's holding the hands of two little girls. One, about four years old, has long, light brown hair and a serious, focused expression, her hand gripping the woman's. The other, perhaps two years old, has slightly darker hair, tied back with a crude ribbon, her head tilted up at the woman, a wide, guileless smile on her face.

## **Signature Item: The Empath's Torc**
### **Lore & Description**
An heirloom piece of jewelry, this elegantly crafted torc of polished electrum is traditionally worn on the wrist by Force-sensitive Zeltrons of Ciara's lineage. Its surface is smooth and cool to the touch, adorned only with a subtle, swirling pattern etched into the metal, mimicking the flow of emotional currents. The torc feels strangely light, yet resonantly alive, thrumming faintly in response to the ebb and flow of emotions in its vicinity. For generations, it has been used to focus the wearer's innate empathy, a conduit that connects them to the emotional well-being of those around them—both a profound comfort and, at times, an overwhelming curse. For Ciara, it is a constant, tangible link to her heritage, a reminder of her unique gifts, and the burden that comes with feeling the galaxy so deeply.

### **Mechanical Properties**
This item is a piece of jewelry and cannot be wielded as a weapon. Its abilities are passive or activated to enhance Ciara's Force connection and empathic capabilities.

*   **Emotional Resonance:** The torc acts as a filter and amplifier for Ciara's powerful Zeltron empathy, allowing her a measure of control over the emotional noise that often plagues her, while simultaneously enhancing her insight into others. Once per encounter, as a **Swift Action**, Ciara can focus through the torc. Make a **DC 15 Use the Force check**. On a success, for the next **1d4 rounds**, Ciara gains a **+2 insight bonus to her Will Defense**, a **+5 equipment bonus on all Sense Motive checks** against organic targets, and any attempt by an enemy within 6 squares to use a [mind-affecting] Force power against her has its **DC increased by 2**.
*   **Heart's Compass:** By consciously attuning herself to the torc, Ciara can extend her empathic senses, seeking out significant emotional undercurrents. This often allows her to discern the presence of potent Light or Dark side influences, or areas of intense peace or turmoil. Once per day, as a **Standard Action**, Ciara can touch the torc and spend a moment in concentration. For the next **1 minute**, she gains a **+5 equipment bonus to Use the Force checks** made to sense others' emotions (e.g., *Sense Force*, *Sense Surroundings*). This provides a general sense of the dominant emotional valence (Light, Dark, peace, turmoil, specific strong emotions) within 100 meters, or aboard a specific vessel she is currently on, but does not give precise locations of individuals. This ability offers broad awareness, not precise targeting.

## **Signature Item: The Empath's Torc**
### **Lore & Description**
An heirloom piece of jewelry, this elegantly crafted torc of polished electrum is traditionally worn on the wrist by Force-sensitive Zeltrons of Ciara's lineage. Its surface is smooth and cool to the touch, adorned only with a subtle, swirling pattern etched into the metal, mimicking the flow of emotional currents. For generations, it has been used not to quiet the emotional currents, but to focus them into a psychic lens. It is a dangerous tool that offers profound insight at the cost of exposing the wearer's mind to the raw, unfiltered chaos of the galaxy. For Ciara, it is a constant, tangible link to her heritage, a reminder that her greatest gift is also her greatest vulnerability.

### **Mechanical Properties**
This item is a piece of jewelry and cannot be wielded as a weapon. Its abilities are passive or activated to enhance Ciara's Force connection and empathic capabilities.

*   **Emotional Focus:** By deliberately opening herself to the emotional chaos, Ciara can gain a moment of stunning insight. Once per encounter, as a **Swift Action**, Ciara can choose to channel the emotional torrent through the torc. She gains a **+5 equipment bonus on a single Sense Motive check** made before the end of her turn.
    *   **Cost:** After the check is resolved, she is struck by psychic backlash from the unfiltered emotional torrent. This backlash makes an attack against her **Will Defense** with an attack bonus of **1d20 + Ciara's level + 2**. If the attack hits, she is overwhelmed and moves **-1 step down the Condition Track**. This is a **Persistent Condition** and requires extended rest (8 hours) to negate. If the attack misses, she successfully weathers the storm with no ill effect.
*   **Heart's Compass:** By consciously attuning herself to the torc, Ciara can extend her empathic senses, seeking out significant emotional undercurrents. This often allows her to discern the presence of potent Light or Dark side influences, or areas of intense peace or turmoil. Once per day, as a **Standard Action**, Ciara can touch the torc and spend a moment in concentration. For the next **1 minute**, she gains a **+5 equipment bonus to Use the Force checks** made to sense others' emotions (e.g., *Sense Force*, *Sense Surroundings*). This provides a general sense of the dominant emotional valence (Light, Dark, peace, turmoil, specific strong emotions) within 100 meters, or aboard a specific vessel she is currently on, but does not give precise locations of individuals. This ability offers broad awareness, not precise targeting.

content: Bleh
!user list
!user details

I do remember having a second Christmas Break one year. M-F and the following M off. That last weekend was a record-setting blizzard. Three feet of snow, and we lived in a valley. Four days of school (T-F) and by then it had all melted and we had major flooding. Another M-F and M off.

That was down south though. Up here, I'm not sure I remember ever having it closed for temps. We definitely did have engines not starting though, so I guess maybe? 🤷
Oh, I haven't run my own car in a couple days. Oops.
I last ran the van on Thursday when I went to work...
We've not had good luck with batteries. They just die out there.
And the 'solution' is to run them for, like, 50min (according to the techs). That's kind of impractical. I do take it for a brief spin though.
When I remember, lol
20minutes of driving or 50 minutes of standby

Which is, I guess, a little cheaper than a new battery but also maybe make batteries that can take the cold temperatures of the places you sell them so we're not spending gas to make up the difference? 🤷
It's just weird. Winter is weird for me, lol
last time I had to replace a battery it was over $100. it sucked
If I made a chair that only works if you took a walk around the block before sitting down, would you still think it was a good deal? lol
Yeah, it was something closer to $200 for us. And it was only a year old (since the last one we had to replace for the same reason).
for me.. the van doesn't have an automaic light switch that will preserve your battery... leaving any sort of light on drains it

Ah. There's maybe two or three weeks a year where the temps get really low (single digits, sometimes below 0) and it just saps the batteries really easily. I'm actually helping at a warming center tonight so folks don't have to sleep outside. It's dangerous.
it's going to be a cold week. I think high of 18 here today.  I'm not leaving the house though so I don't care
also I find it hilarious that one stray comment has led to an entire "Iyola goes to the gym" thread
I think we're all amused

### **Starting Condition: Hibernation Sickness**

You are all awakening from a slumber that has lasted for centuries, and the process has left your bodies and minds in a fragile state. This is represented by a **Persistent Condition** called Hibernation Sickness, which has two primary effects:

### **For Force-Sensitive Characters: The Muted Current**

Beyond the failure of your physical eyes, your connection to the Force feels... distorted. It is as if a thick, heavy fog has settled over your spirit. Reaching for your power results in a jarring sense of resistance and psychic static, making even the simplest intuition a monumental effort.

If you succeed, you can perceive your surroundings through the Force, removing the penalties from blindness on your Perception checks until the start of your next turn.
*   **Sustained Sight:** Outside of combat, one successful check allows you to maintain this Force Sight for about ten minutes before you need to refocus.
*   **Suppression:** Be aware that until your condition improves or the environment changes, your ability to manifest active Force Powers may be significantly hindered or entirely unresponsive.

Hi Anissa,
I wanted to send a follow-up regarding our conversation about Jackson’s behavior on the bus today.
We have already addressed the hitting with Jackson at home and he has been disciplined. We’re making it very clear to him that physical reactions are never the answer, even when he feels pushed. However, when we got his side of the story, he was very frustrated and explained, "She wouldn't keep her hands and feet to herself after I told her to stop, and she just kept doing it." It seems like there is a growing issue with bullying going both ways, and while we are handling Jackson’s part, we don’t really appreciate him being singled out for what is clearly a multi-sided issue.
Since the bus company is currently requiring Jackson to sit in his own seat with a seatbelt, it really highlights a bigger question regarding the safety of all the kids. If Jackson is being buckled in for behavioral reasons, I feel that same standard should be applied to everyone for their physical safety.
The bus uses the highway every day, and we all know that seatbelts are the most effective way to reduce injuries during an accident. The belts are already there and available on the bus, so it seems like a major safety oversight not to use them. We wouldn't dream of letting our children ride in a car without buckling up—why should the bus be any different?
I really believe that universal seatbelt usage and assigned seats would solve several problems at once. It keeps the kids safe in the event of a crash, and it creates the physical boundaries needed to stop these types of altercations before they even start. I’m expecting the bus company to put a plan in place to require seatbelts and assigned seats for all students starting immediately after spring break and carrying over into the next school year.

Because of the complexity of the bullying and these safety concerns, I’d like to have a face-to-face meeting with you to work through these issues together. Please let me know when you have some time for the three of us to sit down and talk.
Best,

~Alicia Dean

I'm asking this around because I saw a video that masterfully and expertly rage baited me, so I want to see the opinion of others as well, it's an hypothetical scenario so bear with me.

So, you and every other person capable of understanding this hypothetical is placed in a room with 2 buttons inside, a Red one and a Blue one.
If the majority pick the Blue one, nothing happens.
If the majority pick the Red one, those that pressed the Blue one are killed.
Everyone can choose freely and understand the situation, also if 100% of people pick the Red button, obviously nobody dies either.

Which button would you press?
what if half choose red and half choose blue? there is no majority?
I guess nothing happens
Or hell coin toss
More fun

if nothing happens and the votes are visible I would say that is as good as a majority decision where nothing happens
shrug
So, Red or Blue?
Do the Blue die instantly or only after everyone has pressed a button?
After the votes are counted I suppose

Even if everyone understands the situation, there will almost certainly be one or two that choose Red but ultimately they’ll be the minority - as long as everyone sees realtime results. It’ll be a larger number if no one sees vote results live. It would be safest for the first person to pick red and for everyone else to also pick red because it will minimize the purposeful contrarians.
What I was thinking.  If you're able to see what the votes are, why not vote the same as the first person? It's dumb unless you actually have a death wish
What if you couldn't see the votes in real time?
then there's a 50/50 of choosing right and I'd choose whichever button was on the right since the majority of people are right handed and it's closer

If you couldn't see the votes but you understood the situation, still go red unless you want to personally perish. On a majority red, you live. On a total red, you live. Or, that's what I'd do anyway. I think. If I understand correctly, lol
What was the rage bait part?
(The part where if one person chooses wrongly they die probably). We're mostly over analyzing to avoid the rage bait
Oh. Ok. This is the most engagement I've had with the server in weeks, lol
The rage part, for me, was most people arguing that Blue is the morally right button to press, because some people may press the Blue button
Where I believe that everyone should just press Red because Blue is the only button that risks you dying

Ah, gotchya. Interesting. There are definitely people who will choose blue early on when there’s still a chance of majority blue because they value guilting others and having that kind of power over literally living but I don’t usually succumb to such tactics, lol
To me it isn't much of a morality, it's just... why risk it ever?
Red doesn't have to kill anyone if people don't take unneccessary risks
People are often irrational, I find, even though it irks me, lol.

I understand if people want to be irrational and moral, because I understand the argument "I would rather risk dying than killing" but the argument I've seen repeated is that pressing the Red button would make you evil incarnate
Which seems a tad excessive
Wow. I hadn’t considered either of those points of view, lol.

I was half asleep when I read the hypothetical, and thus misunderstood, so I would have been excluded from the trial since it specifies it applies to people who are "capable of understanding this hypothetical" lol
I now understand the hypothetical, and your logic, but without the chance for discussion, we won't get 100% red pressed, so I press blue.
I can't know how other people will decide, and we need 100% red for no deaths, and we need 50.01% blue for no deaths.
I can definitely see where people could turn it into a whole thing though.
I get that logic but in my perspective the people that pick blue are taking a risk without a reason to do so, since there is 0 benefits to picking Blue
The only reason to pick Blue is because there may be people that don't understand that picking Blue is only detrimental
And I don't feel I should put myself in danger just because other people do so
Again, I do understand the reasoning of not wanting to hurt others, I just got rage baited because of the whole "YOU'RE A HORRIBLE PERSON IF YOU PICK [X] INSTEAD OF [Y]"

Similarly, houses at the very bottom are between $325K and $350K - but those are 2-3 bedroom, 1 bath, usually no basement or needs work.
Literally, when we told our landlord we'd like to buy, his response was: "On the market, I'll be asking $310K. I've been advised to ask for $380K for a private sale though."

There is/was a push for a bill (I think it didn't get enough votes) that would allow landlords to take additional deposits from tenants when they moved in, which is just... that's the opposite of how to fix a housing crisis, lol. The problem is a) we don't have enough housing, and b) the housing we have is unaffordable. Allowing people to go into more debt and encouraging predatory rental owners isn't the way to fix things. More units, priced according to reality and not some mythical average income, coupled with a push for living wages, is the solution forward. Difficult in a college town, where the counterargument is "Yeah, or just keep renting to groups of 4 and 5 nineteen-year-olds."

I forget the numbers exactly, but a recent article cited something like 53% of rental properties were owned by people who don't live in the city, and a majority of rental properties are owned by just two property management agencies. Like, this is where you focus your efforts if you want to really solve a housing crisis but... 🤷
